speaker: Doctor
text: Greeting, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying these symptoms? Also, does the pain radiate toward your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). Based on your age, the specific combination of visible hematuria and right flank pain, and your history of recurrent UTIs (which can predispose to stone formation), this is the most likely cause. The absence of fever makes an acute pyelonephritis less likely, but please let me know if you experience any shaking chills.
